name: Cal.com
look: White canvas with a black CTA, light-grey cards, real product fragments embedded, and a pill-group nav switcher.

hero.title: Scheduling infrastructure for everyone
hero.sub: The open-source scheduling layer. Use the hosted booking pages, or embed the whole engine in your own product and never send anyone to a third-party link again.

features.title: Booking pages, or the engine underneath
features.sub: Most people want the booking page. Some want the availability engine inside their own product. Both are supported.

items.title: Booking pages
items.body: A shareable link that respects your real availability across every connected calendar.

items.title: Round robin
items.body: Distribute bookings across a team by availability, load or priority.

items.title: 60+ integrations
items.body: Calendars, video tools, payments and CRMs, connected rather than reimplemented.

items.title: Embeddable
items.body: Drop the booker into your own product as a component, styled to your design system.

items.title: Timezone sanity
items.body: Slots shown in the visitor's timezone with daylight-saving handled correctly on both sides.

items.title: Self-hostable
items.body: Run the entire platform on your own infrastructure under an open licence.

showcases.title: Your product, not our subdomain
showcases.body: The booker is a component you can embed and theme, so customers schedule inside your product rather than being handed off to a link that looks like somebody else's brand.
points: React component or plain script embed

showcases.title: Self-host the whole thing
showcases.body: For teams where calendar data cannot leave the perimeter, the entire platform runs on your own infrastructure with the same feature set as the hosted service.

gallery.title: Documentation
gallery.sub: Setup, embedding, the API and self-hosting.

testimonial.quote: We embedded the booker in our onboarding flow in an afternoon. Customers never leave our product, which was the entire reason we stopped using the alternative.
testimonial.name: Laura Simmons

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.sub: Free for individuals. Paid for teams and embedding.

items.a: Yes, and self-hostable in full rather than as a limited community edition. The paid plans add team features and support, not core capability.
Google, Outlook, Office 365, iCloud and CalDAV, with multiple calendars per person merged for availability checking.
Yes, on Platform. Your domain, your branding, and no reference to us anywhere in the booking flow.

items.q: What happens to bookings if I self-host later?
items.a: Export and import are supported both ways. Moving between hosted and self-hosted keeps your event types and history intact.

cta.title: Start scheduling
cta.sub: Free for individuals, open source, and self-hostable.

notes: White canvas with a confident black CTA at 8px and weight-600 labels — the friendly-SaaS button, done precisely.
The display face is geometric and slightly condensed with negative tracking; body stays in a neutral sans.
Light-grey card surfaces carry features, testimonials and non-featured pricing. The featured tier flips to dark — the only dark card on a light page.
Real product fragments — schedule pickers, calendar widgets, integration grids — sit inside marketing cards. The voltage comes from actual product chrome at small scale.
The nav pill-group wrapper around grouped segments is one of the system's signature interactive components.
